title: My early beta roguelike cardgame - How are you leveraging AI to improve balance and game loop mechanics?
author: Final_gamedev
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’m solo-developing a PvE **roguelike deckbuilder**.

It’s currently in super early beta, so I'm pushing big updates every 2-3 days regarding balance, UI/UX, and graphics.

**Key Features:**

\- 15-match runs

\- Card upgrades, fusion mechanics, and relics

\- Minimalist art style (focusing on gameplay loop first)

  
**How I've used AI so far:**

* Brainstorming unique card synergies, relics, and fusion mechanics.
* Drafting initial balancing values and deck progression logic.
* Rapid iteration on UI/UX ideas and minimalist visual assets.

Attached is a 1.5-minute gameplay video.

I’m now looking to take it a step further. **How are other game devs here using AI for deeper game design tasks (like complex balance testing or procedural event generation)?** Any prompts, workflows, or tools you'd recommend?

If you want to see how the game currently plays (or give it a spin), it’s free on Itch: [https://finalstudiodev.itch.io/tenuta](https://finalstudiodev.itch.io/tenuta)

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: I'd have the AI write a headless simulator that plays thousands of 15-match runs with a few simple bot strategies and dumps win rates per card and relic to a CSV. Then you just look for outliers, like cards in way more winning decks than average or ones that never get picked. It won't tell you what's fun, but it catches broken fusions fast so your playtesters can focus on feel.
